Incorporating the SLOOS, the hawkish June 2022 FOMC stance (rate hike to 1.5–1.75% and balance-sheet runoff) still leans restrictive, but bank lending conditions look more supportive than the FSR alone suggests. Banks generally eased standards for C&I loans and multifamily properties, kept construction/land development and other CRE standards largely unchanged, and some reduced costs on credit lines. Loan demand strengthened for inventory, accounts receivable, plant, and equipment financing, and was stronger for HELOCs and auto loans, though demand for RRE mortgages weakened. Foreign banks tightened C&I standards, indicating some cross-border caution. Netting these, credit supply and demand remain relatively resilient, partially offsetting inflation and growth headwinds. Overall tilt remains cautious but less negative than before.
